name: Computational Techniques for Multiphase Flows
description: The course covers fundamentals of multiphase flows, including classification, flow regimes, and applications, followed by continuum formulation using phase indicator functions and volume averaging. Interfacial physics, jump conditions, surface tension, and non-dimensional analysis are introduced before deriving governing transport equations for variable-property single-fluid formulations. Numerical preliminaries include discretization, stability, and property jumps. Interface tracking and capturing approaches are studied in detail: level set method (formulation, reinitialization, mass conservation), volume-of-fluid (VOF) method (interface reconstruction, flux calculation), coupled level set–VOF (CLSVOF), and phase-field methods (Cahn–Hilliard, Allen–Cahn). The course concludes with validation cases, adaptive mesh refinement, and applications to engineering and research problems.
